title: Single-shot coherent process tomography and mid-infrared polarimetry with undetected photons
authors: Marthe Zeja, Wen-Zhe Yan, Zhibo Hou, Sven Ramelow
abstract: Measurements with undetected photons infer properties of a probe beam that is never detected, transferring mid-infrared information onto silicon-friendly wavelengths. Tomography in this paradigm has so far relied on switched settings or scanned phases, referenced across a drift-sensitive campaign; no protocol reads all Jones parameters from one frame. We show that a folded nonlinear interferometer with a diagonally pumped crossed-crystal source performs coherent process tomography of the undetected beam in a single spectrometer frame: it reconstructs all seven parameters of the beam's round-trip Jones matrix, the coherent part of the channel. Birefringent group-delay walk-off, normally a calibration nuisance, acts as a frequency multiplexer: each Jones-matrix element is assigned its own carrier, a spectral fringe period paired with a detector port. Because the multiplexing exploits the down-conversion bandwidth rather than merely tolerating it, a single Fourier transform per detector trace returns all four moduli and all three relative phases across that bandwidth, i.e., the full round-trip Jones spectrum up to a global phase, with no scan or setting change (after a one-time reference frame). Simultaneity makes every relative phase immune to common-mode drift, and a dark carrier, a self-interference term that unitarity forces to vanish, provides a built-in null test. For realistic parameters of a periodically poled KTP source the scheme yields wavelength-resolved mid-infrared polarimetry across 3.5-4.2 microns (~80 spectral points per Jones element) on a silicon camera, extending to depth-resolved Jones matrices, i.e., polarization-sensitive optical coherence tomography with undetected photons. A Fisher-information analysis, the first we are aware of in undetected-photon tomography, sets the precision budget and compares delay multiplexing to sequential protocols at equal photon number.
summary: This paper presents a novel technique for performing coherent process tomography and mid-infrared polarimetry using photons that are never directly measured. By employing a folded nonlinear interferometer and exploiting birefringent walk-off as a frequency multiplexer, the authors read all necessary polarization parameters simultaneously in a single measurement frame. This breakthrough enables broadband, drift-immune characterization of optical channels, extending to depth-resolved polarimetry.
main_problem: Developing a method for single-shot coherent process tomography and mid-infrared polarimetry using light that is never directly detected (undetected photons).
main_result: The authors demonstrate a protocol that reconstructs all seven parameters of the beam's round-trip Jones matrix in a single spectrometer frame, achieving wavelength-resolved mid-IR polarimetry.
method: A folded nonlinear interferometer pumped diagonally is used, where birefringent group-delay walk-off acts as a frequency multiplexer to read all Jones parameters simultaneously via a single Fourier transform.
model_or_system: The experiment utilizes a folded nonlinear interferometer with a diagonally pumped crossed-crystal source (ppKTP) to probe the unknown channel's round-trip Jones matrix M. The measurement transfers mid-infrared information onto silicon-friendly wavelengths.
key_observables: The full complex Jones spectrum M(lambda), including all four moduli and three relative phases across the bandwidth.
important_parameters: The seven real parameters defining the Jones matrix M; the spectral bandwidth (3.5-4.2 microns); and the photon number N for precision analysis.
main_assumptions: The technique relies on the multiplexing capability provided by birefringent group-delay walk-off and assumes the validity of the Fisher-information analysis for this novel measurement scheme.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the folded nonlinear interferometer setup, detailing components like QWP/HWP and the crossed-crystal source.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem of single-shot tomography, details the folded interferometer setup and the multiplexing mechanism, presents the results for reconstructing the full Jones spectrum, and concludes with a Fisher-information analysis comparing the new method to sequential protocols.
why_interesting: This work represents a significant advancement in quantum optics measurement techniques, providing a robust, single-shot, and drift-immune method for characterizing complex quantum channels using non-detected light.
